title: The Board of Peace announces a 15-point roadmap for phased disarmament of Hamas
body:
On 30 July 2026, US President Donald Trump said the American-led Board of Peace had reached a historic agreement for the phased disarmament of Hamas, according to FDD's Long War Journal. The 15-point roadmap would transfer civilian and security governance from Hamas to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), supported by the International Stabilization Force, which had not yet deployed. The Israel Defense Forces and Hamas would cease military operations, and an implementation mechanism would be prepared within 14 days.

After that period the NCAG would enter Gaza and take over government institutions, public services, police, weapons licensing and internal security. An International Verification Committee of Board of Peace representatives, guarantor states and the stabilization force would certify each side's compliance at each stage. Hamas weapons would be gradually decommissioned and stored by the NCAG, tied to a phased Israeli withdrawal, and the stabilization force would separate the IDF from NCAG-controlled areas. Washington's preliminary estimate was seven to eight months.

Sequencing was disputed. An Israeli official told Reuters there would be no withdrawal until Hamas underwent genuine disarmament. Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad called the roadmap difficult and painful and said Hamas would not begin disarming until Israel halted operations, increased aid and fully withdrew. US officials said Israel was very skeptical that Hamas would give up its weapons. The IDF reported 32 strikes and ceasefire-related actions between 10 and 31 July 2026, figures that were not independently verified.
